manifest.title: Headscale
manifest.author: Marcus Quinn <marcus@marcusquinn.com>
manifest.description:
Headscale is an open-source, self-hosted implementation of the Tailscale
control server. Devices run the official Tailscale apps and join a private
WireGuard mesh (a "tailnet") that your Cloudron coordinates, instead of
Tailscale's hosted service.

### Features

* **Official Tailscale clients** on Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS and Android,
  pointed at your server with `--login-server`.
* **Direct WireGuard connections** between devices, with NAT traversal.
* **Embedded DERP relay** for devices that cannot connect directly. Tailscale's
  public relays stay available as a fallback.
* **MagicDNS** names for every device, plus ACL policies, tags, subnet routers
  and exit nodes.
* **Pre-auth keys** for servers and devices that cannot open a browser.

### Cloudron integration

* **Single sign-on:** `tailscale up` opens a Cloudron login. The app's access
  control decides who can add devices.
* **One HTTPS address:** control traffic, the Noise protocol and the DERP relay
  all use the app's HTTPS domain. One extra UDP port carries STUN.
* **Backups:** the SQLite database, keys and `config.yaml` in `/app/data` are
  in Cloudron backups.

Headscale has no web interface. Manage users, devices, keys and routes with the
`headscale` command in the app's Terminal.

[Headscale](https://github.com/juanfont/headscale) is open source under the
BSD-3-Clause licence. This package is maintained independently of the
Headscale project and is not affiliated with Tailscale Inc.
manifest.tagline: Self-hosted Tailscale control server with SSO and a DERP relay

STUN_PORT.title: STUN (NAT traversal)
STUN_PORT.description: UDP port for the embedded DERP relay's STUN service. Disabling it also disables the embedded relay; devices then use Tailscale's public relays. Avoid 3478 (Cloudron TURN) and ports other apps use.

manifest.postInstallMessage:
Headscale is running. It has no web interface; devices connect with the
Tailscale app and you manage it from the app's Terminal.

<sso>
**Add a device:** run

    tailscale up --login-server https://$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN

and sign in with your Cloudron account in the browser that opens. Every
Cloudron user allowed by this app's access control can add devices. On macOS,
iOS and Windows, set the server under the app's alternate coordination server
option; see `https://$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN/apple` and `/windows`.
</sso>

<nosso>
**Add a device:** in the Terminal, create a user, find its ID, and create a
pre-auth key for that ID:

    headscale users create alice
    headscale users list
    headscale preauthkeys create --user <ID> --expiration 1h

then on the device run
`tailscale up --login-server https://$CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN --authkey <key>`.
</nosso>

**Servers and headless devices:** use a pre-auth key as above. List devices
with `headscale nodes list`.

**STUN port:** if your server sits behind a provider firewall, allow the UDP
port shown under *Location*, so devices can find direct paths and use the
embedded relay.

Settings live in `/app/data/config.yaml`; restart after editing. Setup guide:
[README](https://github.com/marcusquinn/cloudron-headscale-app/blob/main/README.md).
manifest.changelog:
* Initial Cloudron package for Headscale 0.29.5.
* Sign in with Cloudron (OIDC) when adding devices; pre-auth keys for headless devices.
* Embedded DERP relay over HTTPS, with STUN on UDP 3480 by default.
* SQLite database, keys and config.yaml in /app/data, included in backups.
